title: Sequence Clustering
text: build_clusters() computes distance every pair sequences groups sequences close (Saqr, López-Pernas, Helske, et al. 2024). takes network, stores sequences, sequences . default uses Hamming distance, number positions two sequences differ (Hamming 1950), partitions sequences around medoids (PAM; Kaufman & Rousseeuw 1990), cluster represented central sequence. print shows cluster’s size, mean within-cluster distance medoid, average silhouette width, compares sequence’s distance cluster distance nearest one: near 1 well-separated clusters, near 0 overlapping ones (Rousseeuw 1987). three clusters hold 183, 106 140 sessions, silhouette 0.22. dissimilarity selects distance (Studer & Ritschard 2016): method selects clustering: "pam" (default) hierarchical clustering, merges closest sequences groups step step: "ward.D2" (Ward’s criterion, Ward 1963, implemented Murtagh & Legendre 2014), "ward.D", "complete", "average", "single", "mcquitty" "centroid". Hamming distance can also weight positions (weighted = TRUE, lambda setting fast weight decays), early differences count .
code: clusters_hamming <- build_clusters(net, k = 3) clusters_hamming #> Sequence Clustering [pam] #>   Sequences: 429  |  Clusters: 3 #>   Dissimilarity: hamming #>   Quality: silhouette = 0.215 #>  #>   Cluster  N            Mean within-dist  Medoid #>   1        183 (42.7%)  7.345             111 #>   2        106 (24.7%)  52.766            282 #>   3        140 (32.6%)  14.881            265

title: Sequence Clustering
text: mixture Markov model groups sequences transitions: fits one Markov chain per cluster assigns sequence chain probably generated (Helske et al. 2024). compare_mmm() fits model several numbers clusters compares BIC (Schwarz 1978), AIC ICL (Biernacki, Celeux & Govaert 2000), lower better, average posterior probability assigned cluster (AvePP). model estimated 50 random starts; seed makes reproducible.  BIC ICL lowest two clusters, also highest AvePP (0.80). AIC keeps decreasing clusters, five-cluster model converge. first cluster (155 sessions) evaluation followed another evaluation probability 0.47 directive evaluation probability 0.30. second (274 sessions) directives follow directives (0.65) metacognitive actions follow metacognitive actions (0.31) often. model cosine clustering describe similar division: sessions alternate directing evaluating, sessions mostly direct.  average posterior probability 0.83 first cluster 0.77 second, 20% sessions expected misclassified. posterior plot shows cluster’s distribution sessions’ posterior probabilities; mass near 1 means clear assignments.  cluster_mmm() fits model returns net_mmm object; name mixture model reached cluster_network().

title: Higher-Order Network Analysis with Simplicial Complexes
text: network describes pairs states (Saqr, López-Pernas, Conde-González, & Hernández-García, 2024). simplicial complex also describes groups: two connected states form 1-simplex (edge), three mutually connected states 2-simplex (filled triangle), k + 1 mutually connected states k-simplex (Battiston et al., 2020). build_simplicial() builds clique complex, every group mutually connected states simplex. Two states connected transition , either direction, probability least threshold. threshold decides transitions count. 0.05 every pair nine actions connected complex single 8-simplex, describes nothing; 0.12 complex keeps frequent transitions. complex 9 states, 16 edges 6 filled triangles, larger groups. title: Comparing Sequences Between Groups: Early vs Late Human-AI Interactions
text: human_long holds coded human turns 429 human-AI pair-programming (“vibe coding”) sessions across 34 projects, one row per coded action (Saqr, Misiejuk & López-Pernas 2026; Misiejuk et al. 2026). nine action codes grouped three clusters, Directive, Evaluative Metacognitive, column cluster, state used . order_in_session gives position action within session. mark_phases() orders actions session order_in_session divides consecutive phases nearly equal length. n = 2, first half session labelled early second half late; odd number actions, middle one belongs second half. build_network() group = "phase" estimates one transition network per half keeps half-session sequences, every function reads. 425 early 429 late half-sessions; four sessions single action early half.
code: library(Nestimate) halves <- mark_phases(human_long, actor = "session_id",                       time = "order_in_session", n = 2,                       labels = c("early", "late")) net <- build_network(halves, actor = "session_id", action = "cluster",                      group = "phase", method = "relative") net #> Group Networks (2 groups, group_col: phase) #>  #>   Group  Nodes  Edges  Weights #>   early  3      9      [0.105, 0.637] #>   late   3      9      [0.131, 0.575]

title: Comparing Sequences Between Groups: Early vs Late Human-AI Interactions
text: first comparison concerns share state, ignoring order. sequence_plot() type = "distribution" shows share state position half-sessions. na = FALSE shares taken among observed actions, trim = 0.9 keeps positions hold 90% actions, since half-sessions longer.  Early halves start almost entirely directives; late halves start three states, metacognitive actions take larger share late halves. mosaic_test() cross-tabulates half state tests association every method clustered counts. actor = "session_id", sessions clusters. Pearson chi-square test treats 10,796 actions independent. Rao-Scott test corrects clustering second-order adjustment (Rao & Scott 1984); design effect, 1.21, factor clustering inflates variance. Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratifies session compares halves within 421 sessions (Landis, Heyman & Koch 1978). GEE test uses cluster-robust covariance (Liang & Zeger 1986), GLMM test mixed model random intercept per session. Donner-Klar test needs one variable constant within cluster (Donner & Klar 1994), half varies within every session, computed. four tests apply reject independence (Rao-Scott F(1.97, 844.7) = 28.72, CMH = 74.24, GEE = 58.17, GLMM = 69.34; every p < 0.001).  mosaic plot, width column share actions half height tile share state within half. fill standardised residual: blue tiles hold actions independence predicts red tiles fewer. Directives -represented early; evaluations metacognitive actions late.

what: The entropy of a transition network
title: Transition Matrix Entropy
text: transition_entropy() accepts fitted network, transition matrix, sequence data. call computes entropy rate HH, stationary entropy H(π)H(\pi) (ceiling apply consecutive actions independent), difference, redundancy. process runs 2.41 bits per step ceiling log⁡29=3.17\log_2 9 = 3.17; normalized entropy 0.76 scale-free version Krejtz et al. (2025) report. Regulation far scripted, knowing current action removes 13% uncertainty next one (relative redundancy 0.134, 0.373 2.78 bits H(π)H(\pi)): sequence carries real information, empirical justification modeling transitions rather activity frequencies alone.
code: library(Nestimate) net <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "relative",                      actor = "Actor", action = "Action", time = "Time") te <- transition_entropy(net) te #> Transition Entropy (9 states, bits; ceiling = 3.170) #>  #>                           raw            normalised #>   Entropy rate    h(P)  = 2.409 bits    0.760 #>   Stationary    H(pi)  = 2.782 bits    0.878 #>   Redundancy   H(pi)-h = 0.373 bits    0.134 #>  #> Normalised: h(P) and H(pi) are raw / log_2(n_states) (0 = deterministic, 1 = uniform); #>   redundancy is the relative redundancy (H(pi) - h(P)) / H(pi), not raw / log_2(n_states).

title: Transition Matrix Entropy
text: Plug-entropy biased small samples (Paninski, 2003) treats edge observed three times exactly like one observed three thousand times. entropy_bayes() places independent Dirichlet posterior row transition matrix (Jeffreys (1946) prior, 0.5, default) pushes Monte Carlo draws entropy formula, every quantity — entropy rate, state’s branching entropy, edge’s contribution — arrives credible interval reflects much data supports . posterior mean (2.411 bits) sits next plug-estimate (2.409): 27,533 actions every row matrix well populated, posterior adds little beyond interval, quantifies firmly data pin process entropy. sparse data two move apart, posterior integrates count uncertainty instead taking point estimate face value. edge flagged credible share HH credibly exceeds min_share (1% default). result also carries entropy network edges zeroed — stable entropy skeleton, safe display without overreading thin cells.  Blue intervals stable estimates; grey intervals rest observations distinguish entropy share noise 95% level.
code: eb <- entropy_bayes(net, draws = 1000, seed = 1) eb #> Bayesian Transition Entropy (9 states, bits; Dirichlet prior 0.5, 1000 draws) #>  #>   entropy_rate:       2.411 [2.396, 2.425] #>   stationary_entropy: 2.783 [2.771, 2.796] #>   redundancy:         0.373 [0.361, 0.384] #>  #> Edges: 78 observed; 31 credible (share of h(P) credibly > 1%). #> Use summary() for the edge table and plot() for the posterior. plot(eb)

title: Network Estimation and Analysis with Nestimate
text: Psychological network analysis estimates conditional dependency structure among set variables (Borsboom et al., 2021; Epskamp & Fried, 2018). Variables (e.g., symptoms, traits, behaviors) represented nodes, edges represent partial correlations — association two variables controlling others. approach reveals variables directly connected versus whose association mediated variables (Saqr et al., 2024). Nestimate supports three estimation methods continuous psychological data, accessed build_network() interface (binary data use method = "ising", mixed continuous categorical data method = "mgm"): Correlation networks (method = "cor") estimate pairwise Pearson correlations produce fully connected undirected networks. informative starting point, distinguish direct indirect associations. Partial correlation networks (method = "pcor") control variables, revealing direct associations. provide accurate picture dependency structure, though results can noisy small samples. Regularized networks via EBICglasso (method = "glasso") apply L1 regularization precision matrix, shrinking weak unreliable edges exactly zero. recommended approach psychological network analysis, balances model fit complexity produces sparse, interpretable, replicable structures.

what: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Network estimation, comparison testing sequence, event-log, panel cross-sectional data. Nestimate estimates, compares tests networks sequence, event-log, panel cross-sectional data. One function, build_network(), gives 15 estimators: transition, frequency, co-occurrence, attention, n-gram, gap, reply latency networks, two window-based networks one-hot data, correlation, partial correlation, graphical lasso, Ising mixed graphical models. Bootstrap intervals, permutation tests, split-half reliability centrality stability apply every network whose data can resampled. functions cover sequence patterns indices, transition entropy, Markov chains, stability landscapes, clustering, mixture Markov models higher-order networks.

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Network estimation analysis Nestimate Transition matrix entropy Markov stability analysis Comparing sequences groups Sequence plots Sequence clustering Network estimation visualization Nestimate + cograph Higher-order network analysis simplicial complexes Model assessment transition networks Nested sequences permutation test Comparing networks compare_networks() Stability engagement: states, landscapes students Function reference

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
code: # From CRAN install.packages("Nestimate")  # Development version devtools::install_github("mohsaqr/Nestimate")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_network() reads event log action, actor time columns named, wide sequences (one row per sequence, one column per position) .
code: library(Nestimate)  net <- build_network(human_long, method = "tna",                      action = "code", actor = "session_id", time = "timestamp")  # One network per group: high and low achievers group_nets <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "tna",                             action = "Action", actor = "Actor",                             time = "Time", group = "Achiever")  # Replies weighted by how fast they came latency <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "latency",                          action = "Action", actor = "Actor", time = "Time")  list_estimators()

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: mark_phases() splits actor’s events n phases, build_network(group = "phase") turns one network per phase.
code: halves <- mark_phases(human_long, actor = "session_id",                       time = "order_in_session", n = 2,                       labels = c("early", "late")) phase_nets <- build_network(halves, method = "relative", actor = "session_id",                             action = "cluster", time = "order_in_session",                             group = "phase")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: wtna() builds networks one-hot data time windows: transitions windows, co-occurrence within windows, .
code: net_wtna  <- wtna(learning_activities, actor = "student",                   method = "transition", type = "relative") net_mixed <- wtna(learning_activities, actor = "student",                   method = "both", type = "relative")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: cooccurrence() builds undirected co-occurrence networks six input formats (delimited fields, long, binary matrix, wide sequences, lists) eight similarity measures (Jaccard, cosine, association strength, Dice others; van Eck & Waltman, 2009).
code: # Codes that occur in the same session net_co <- cooccurrence(human_long, field = "code", by = "session_id",                        similarity = "jaccard", threshold = 0.1)

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: graphical lasso, Ising mixed graphical models estimated ‘psychnets’ package.
code: net_gl <- build_network(srl_strategies, method = "glasso") net_gl  predictability(net_gl)   # variance of each node explained by its neighbours

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_mlvar() estimates three networks experience-sampling data: Temporal (directed): lagged fixed effects Contemporaneous (undirected): partial correlations within-person residuals -person (undirected): partial correlations person means estimates equal mlVAR::mlVAR() estimator = "lmer" fixed temporal contemporaneous effects. data one row per beep (id, optional day, beep variables); ?build_mlvar runnable simulated panel.
code: # esm: one row per person and beep, columns id, day, beep, happy, calm, tired fit <- build_mlvar(esm, vars = c("happy", "calm", "tired"),                    id = "id", day = "day", beep = "beep")  fit           # the temporal, contemporaneous and between-person networks summary(fit) coefs(fit)    # one row per edge: beta, SE, t, p and interval

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_gimme() estimates network person GIMME (Group Iterative Multiple Model Estimation), paths shared group paths person.
code: # panel: one row per person and time point, columns id, V1, ..., V4 (see ?build_gimme) fit_g <- build_gimme(panel, vars = c("V1", "V2", "V3", "V4"), id = "id") fit_g   # group paths and the network of each person

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_clusters() partitions sequences k groups distance matrix (9 distances; PAM 8 hierarchical linkages). cluster_choice() compares numbers clusters. result build_clusters() build_mmm() passed build_network() gives one network per cluster.
code: clust <- build_clusters(net, k = 3, dissimilarity = "hamming", method = "ward.D2") plot(clust, type = "silhouette") cluster_nets <- build_network(clust, method = "tna")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_mmm() fits mixture Markov chains EM; compare_mmm() gives BIC, AIC ICL per number components.
code: mmm <- build_mmm(net, k = 3) compare_mmm(net, k = 2:4) mmm_nets <- build_network(mmm, method = "tna")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: build_mcml() splits network -cluster (macro) within-cluster layers states belong known groups, three code families human_long.
code: families <- list(Directive     = c("Command", "Request", "Specify"),                  Evaluative    = c("Correct", "Frustrate", "Refine", "Verify"),                  Metacognitive = c("Inquire", "Interrupt")) mcml <- build_mcml(human_long, clusters = families, action = "code",                    actor = "session_id", time = "timestamp") summary(mcml)          # within and between totals per family macro_network(mcml)    # the family-level transition network

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
code: hon  <- build_hon(net, max_order = 2) pathways(hon)                      # paths in arrow notation hypa <- build_hypa(net) summary(hypa)                      # over- and under-represented paths with p-values

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Simplicial complexes built network: Betti numbers, Euler characteristic, persistent homology across thresholds Atkin’s Q-analysis.
code: sc <- build_simplicial(net, type = "clique") betti_numbers(sc)          # components, cycles, voids euler_characteristic(sc) ph <- persistent_homology(net) plot(ph) qa <- q_analysis(sc)       # Q-connectivity structure vectors

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Index plots state distributions, whole data, group cluster.
code: sequence_plot(net)                       # one row per sequence, sorted by similarity sequence_plot(clust, type = "index")     # one panel per cluster distribution_plot(net, geom = "area")    # state distribution over positions sequence_plot(daily_actions, actor = "student", action = "action",               periods = "day")           # actions per day

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: sequence_patterns() counts contiguous, gapped repeated patterns tests groups. sequence_metrics() computes 23 indices per sequence (entropy, turbulence, complexity, spells others) compares groups. sequence_compare() tests k-gram frequencies groups.
code: sequence_patterns(trajectories, len = 2:3, top = 10) sequence_patterns(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor", action = "Action",                   time = "Time", len = 2, group = "Achiever", top = 10)  sequence_metrics(trajectories) sequence_metrics(phase_nets, iter = 99)     # early versus late halves  res <- sequence_compare(group_nets, sub = 2:4, test = "chisq", adjust = "fdr") res                                 # one row per pattern and group, rounded summary(res)                        # every row as a data frame plot(res)                           # back-to-back pyramid

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: transition_entropy() gives entropy rate transition network state’s share (Cover & Thomas, 2006; Krejtz et al., 2015). entropy_trajectory() follows entropy sliding windows, bootstrap band per group.
code: traj_net <- build_network(trajectories, method = "relative") te <- transition_entropy(traj_net) te summary(te)  tr <- entropy_trajectory(group_regulation_long, action = "Action",                          actor = "Actor", time = "Time", group = "Achiever") plot(tr)

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: markov_order_test() tests many previous states next one depends . markov_stability() reports, per state, persistence, sojourn time, stationary probability, return time quickly reached states. passage_time() gives mean first-passage time every pair states, chain_structure() communicating classes absorption.
code: markov_order_test(trajectories, max_order = 2, n_perm = 99, seed = 1)  stab <- markov_stability(net) summary(stab)             # one row per state plot(stab)  pt <- passage_time(net) pt                        # expected steps from state i to state j  chain_structure(traj_net)

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: stability_landscape() draws state cup whose depth log expected stay , bootstrap intervals. landscape_trend() follows depths windows positions along covariate.
code: land <- stability_landscape(traj_net,   states = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"), iter = 50, seed = 1) land plot(land)  trend <- landscape_trend(traj_net, along = "phase",   states = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"), iter = 50, seed = 1) plot(trend)

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: compare_networks() compares every pair networks group: edge, node global differences, permutation Bayesian test. permutation() tests edge differences two networks, nct() Network Comparison Test psychological networks (van Borkulo et al., 2022).
code: courses <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "relative",                          actor = "Actor", action = "Action", time = "Time",                          group = "Course") cmp <- compare_networks(courses) summary(cmp) edge_differences(cmp, pair = c("A", "B")) plot(cmp, type = "difference")  perm <- permutation(group_nets, iter = 1000) summary(perm)  nct_res <- nct(head(srl_strategies, 125), tail(srl_strategies, 125), iter = 500) nct_res                   # structure, global strength and edge tests

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: mosaic_test() tests state--group table counts nested actors (Rao-Scott, Donner-Klar, CMH, GEE mixed model); mosaic_plot() draws residuals.
code: counts <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "frequency",                         actor = "Actor", action = "Action", time = "Time") mosaic_test(counts, method = c("chisq", "rao_scott"), actor = "Group")

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: association_rules() mines “B” rules sequences binary matrices Apriori algorithm, support, confidence, lift conviction.
code: rules <- association_rules(net, min_support = 0.05, min_confidence = 0.6) summary(rules)                    # one row per rule, sorted by lift pathways(rules)                   # rules in arrow notation

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: predict_links() scores every unobserved pair states structural similarity; evaluate_links() gives AUC, precision recall held-edges.
code: # Keep transitions with probability >= 0.1, then predict the rest sparse <- build_network(human_long, method = "tna", action = "code",                         actor = "session_id", time = "timestamp",                         threshold = 0.1) preds <- predict_links(sparse)    # common neighbours, Adamic-Adar, Katz, ... summary(preds)  # Do the predictions recover the transitions between 0.05 and 0.1 that were cut? evaluate_links(preds, extract_edges(net, threshold = 0.05))

title: Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
text: Bootstrap intervals, split-half reliability centrality stability resample sequences actors. apply every network whose data can resampled; latency networks take bootstrap, one-hot data need actor session resample.
code: boot <- bootstrap_network(net, iter = 1000) summary(boot)  network_reliability(net)          # split-half reliability centrality_stability(net)         # CS-coefficient by case-dropping  boot_gl <- boot_glasso(net_gl, iter = 1000) summary(boot_gl)                  # edge inclusion and centrality intervals

title: Convert an action column to one-hot columns — action_to_onehot
text: action_to_onehot() adds one 0/1 indicator column per state data frame categorical action column: column row's state 1 others 0. result one-hot layout build_network() reads codes format = "onehot", wtna() reads directly.

title: Convert an action column to one-hot columns — action_to_onehot
code: action_to_onehot(   data,   action_col = "Action",   states = NULL,   drop_action = TRUE,   sort_states = FALSE,   prefix = "" )

title: Convert an action column to one-hot columns — action_to_onehot
text: data data frame action column. action_col action column. Default "Action"; name column raises error. states states make columns , order. Default NULL, every non-missing value action column order first appearance. listed state never occurs gets column zeros, row whose state listed 0 every column. drop_action Whether remove action column. Default TRUE. sort_states Whether sort state columns alphabetically (level order factor action column). Default FALSE. prefix prefix state column names. Without one, state named like existing column replaces column. Default "".

title: Convert an action column to one-hot columns — action_to_onehot
text: input data frame one integer column per state appended, named paste0(prefix, state). columns kept; action column removed unless drop_action = FALSE. row missing action NA every state column.

title: Convert an action column to one-hot columns — action_to_onehot
code: long_data <- data.frame(   Actor = rep(1:3, each = 4),   Time = rep(1:4, 3),   Action = sample(c("A", "B", "C"), 12, replace = TRUE) ) onehot_data <- action_to_onehot(long_data) head(onehot_data) #>   Actor Time A C B #> 1     1    1 1 0 0 #> 2     1    2 0 1 0 #> 3     1    3 0 1 0 #> 4     1    4 1 0 0 #> 5     2    1 0 0 1 #> 6     2    2 0 1 0

code: # A three-variable ESM panel: 20 people x 20 beeps. `tired` is driven by # `happy` one beep earlier, so the temporal network should recover it. if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   n_beep <- 20   ar1 <- function(n, phi) as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(n), phi,                                                    method = "recursive"))   panel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(i) {     happy <- ar1(n_beep, 0.4)     data.frame(       id    = i,       beep  = seq_len(n_beep),       happy = happy + stats::rnorm(1),       calm  = ar1(n_beep, 0.3) + stats::rnorm(1),       tired = 0.5 * c(0, happy[-n_beep]) + stats::rnorm(n_beep) +               stats::rnorm(1)     )   }))   fit <- build_mlvar(panel, vars = c("happy", "calm", "tired"),                      id = "id", beep = "beep")   fit   coefs(fit)   summary(fit) } #> === mlVAR Summary === #> Subjects: 20  | Observations: 380  | Variables: 3  | Lag: 1  #> Standardized: FALSE  #>  #> --- Temporal Network (rows: predictor at t - lag; Printing summary shows counts integers metrics four significant digits.

title: Build a simplicial complex — build_simplicial
text: build_simplicial() builds simplicial complex, higher-order structure network: besides nodes (0-simplices) edges (1-simplices) holds filled triangles (2-simplices), tetrahedra larger groups nodes. Three constructions available type: Clique complex ("clique"): every clique network whose edges reach threshold becomes simplex, standard bridge graph algebraic topology. Pathway complex ("pathway"): states higher-order pathway net_hon, net_hypa net_mogen (one built tna model netobject) become simplex. Vietoris-Rips complex ("vr", alias "rips"): input non-negative distance matrix, every group nodes whose pairwise distances max_scale becomes simplex, simplex records scale enters (largest pairwise distance), persistent_homology() can read filtration. clique complex fixed thresholded graph, since every clique filled ; Betti numbers count holes remain, cycles edges triangles fill. shape depends threshold, read betti_numbers() one threshold, follow features across persistent_homology(). pathway complex built paths observed sequences, simplices say states occur together path. simplicial_degree() q_analysis() describe nodes take part complex.

code: # A three-variable ESM panel: 20 people x 20 beeps. `tired` is driven by # `happy` one beep earlier, so the temporal network should recover it. if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   n_beep <- 20   ar1 <- function(n, phi) as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(n), phi,                                                    method = "recursive"))   panel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(i) {     happy <- ar1(n_beep, 0.4)     data.frame(       id    = i,       beep  = seq_len(n_beep),       happy = happy + stats::rnorm(1),       calm  = ar1(n_beep, 0.3) + stats::rnorm(1),       tired = 0.5 * c(0, happy[-n_beep]) + stats::rnorm(n_beep) +               stats::rnorm(1)     )   }))   fit <- build_mlvar(panel, vars = c("happy", "calm", "tired"),                      id = "id", beep = "beep")   fit   coefs(fit)   summary(fit) } #> === mlVAR Summary === #> Subjects: 20  | Observations: 380  | Variables: 3  | Lag: 1  #> Standardized: FALSE  #>  #> --- Temporal Network (rows: predictor at t - lag; "bootstrap" runs vertex bootstrap vertex_compare() per pair adds structural rows (density, mean weight, centralization , directed networks, reciprocity) global table, boot_observed_a, boot_observed_b, boot_se, boot_ci_lower, boot_ci_upper, boot_z, boot_p boot_sig. reads weights, plain matrices support ; two tests need build_network() output data, tna models, rebuilt sequences reproduce weights. sig evidence columns take permutation result run (edge node tables), otherwise Bayesian one (edge table ).

text:
Clique-motif eigenvector centrality (CEC) leading eigenvector clique-expanded pairwise graph \(W\) \(W_{ij} = |\{e : , j \e\}|\), number hyperedges two nodes share. reads membership (positive incidence cell, rule builds $hyperedges), incidence weights ignored: equals igraph::eigen_centrality() clique_expansion(hg, weighted = FALSE), clique_expansion()'s default output unweighted hypergraph. vector solved directly symmetric eigendecomposition connected component (Perron-Frobenius makes leading eigenvalue connected component simple), power iteration, oscillates clique expansion bipartite (example star pairs). several components share largest eigenvalue, result projection uniform vector onto joint leading eigenspace; components smaller leading eigenvalue score zero. Z-eigenvector centrality (ZEC) solves eigen-equation hyperedge tensor, $$\lambda\, x_i \;=\; \sum_{e 
i }\; \prod_{j \e,\; j 
eq } x_j,$$ shifted power iteration (variant SS-HOPM, Kolda & Mayo, 2011, normalises tensor step adding shift). Tensor products normalisation evaluated log space, centralities stay finite normalised large hyperedges. Besides step tolerance, iteration checks eigen-equation residual small (relative residual max(sqrt(tol), 1e-6)); otherwise warns. H-eigenvector centrality (HEC) solves, iteration, $$\lambda\, x_i^{k-1} \;=\; \sum_{e 
i }\; \prod_{j \e,\; j 
eq } x_j.$$ Uniform hypergraphs . Benson (2019) defines ZEC HEC \(k\)-uniform hypergraphs. mixed sizes right-hand side mixes polynomial degrees, equation scale-free solution: vector satisfies normalisation chosen inside iteration. Hyperedges one member contribute nothing ignored uniformity check. mixed sizes use "clique", keep one size build_hypergraph() (include_pairwise = FALSE). Disconnected hypergraphs. Z-eigenvector unique hypergraph several components: different iterations can solve equation different vectors, compare "Z" values within one connected hypergraph .

what: Compute the transition entropy of a Markov chain — transition_entropy
title: Compute the transition entropy of a Markov chain — transition_entropy
text: transition_entropy() measures uncertain Markov chain's next step , three levels: branching entropy state (evenly outgoing transitions spread), entropy stationary distribution, chain's entropy rate, average uncertainty per step. takes transition network, tna model, transition matrix wide sequence data; netobject_group gives one result per group. entropy rate $$h(P) = -\sum_i \pi_i \sum_j P_{ij} \log_b P_{ij},$$ \(\pi\) stationary distribution, per-step uncertainty chain's trajectories (Cover & Thomas, 2006, ch. 4). introduced behavioural research gaze transition entropy Krejtz et al. (2015) tracked real time mobile transition matrix entropy Krejtz et al. (2025). normalised values divide \(\log_b n\), entropy uniform branching among \(n\) states; scale-free variants papers report. entropy rate near 0 means current state almost fixes next one; near ceiling \(\log_b n\) (normalised 1), every next state equally likely. redundancy \(H(\pi) - h(P)\) uncertainty knowing current state removes, zero successive states independent. point estimates one transition matrix: entropy_bayes() gives credible intervals, entropy_network() shows transitions carry entropy, entropy_trajectory() changes time. chain one closed class one stationary distribution; check classes chain_structure().

title: Nestimate 1.1.4
text: Latency networks. build_network(method = "latency") builds reply network faster replies carry weight (Templeton et al. 2022). Stability landscapes. stability_landscape() draws state cup whose depth shows long people stay . landscape_trend() follows depths time along covariate, landscape_surface() draws along measure stability. Sequence patterns indices. sequence_patterns() finds patterns sequences tests groups. sequence_metrics() computes 23 indices sequence (entropy, turbulence, complexity, spells others) compares groups. pattern_outcome() relates patterns outcome, extract_sequences() returns sequences behind input. Phases. mark_phases() splits person’s events phases, build_network(group = "phase") gives one network per phase. Nested data. mosaic_test() tests counts nested people teams, mosaic_plot() mosaic_analysis() take nested actor. permutation(), centrality_stability() casedrop_reliability() take actor resample whole people. Entropy time. entropy_trajectory() reads sequences well event logs, plot shows bootstrap band around trend. Sequence plots period. sequence_plot() can show actions per day, week month (periods), sequence_plot() distribution_plot() can drop rare columns (trim). tna models can passed wherever network sequences accepted. New dataset daily_actions: learning actions 30 students seven days (simulated). Smaller additions: node_clusters(), label_predictions() label_scores(); nct() handles missing values constant variables; extract_edges() extract_initial_probs() read group networks; build_*() shortcuts take group, scaling, threshold params; build_mcml() reads edge lists; cooccurrence() association_rules() read 0/1 tables (format = "binary"); compare_networks() marks significant differences difference plot; window_size build_network(params = ) now works tna.
